Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Consistent assessment findings:
  - Intermittent headaches with frontal location and nausea; episodes occurred mainly during work and with computer-based tasks
  - Systemic symptoms including heat sensation, tachycardia, shortness of breath at desk, reduced appetite with unintentional weight loss (~5 lb), and decreased libido
  - Tingling in both arms; no leg paresthesias
  - Known hyperthyroidism on thyroxine with reported adherence
  - Significant work-related stress (7–8/10)
  - Plan to perform in-clinic examination (heart and lungs) and arrange blood tests focusing on thyroid function
- Differential diagnoses consistent with transcript and DDx:
  - Thyrotoxicosis / Hyperthyroidism (likely related to thyroxine therapy; over-replacement or increased sensitivity) — High likelihood
  - Migraine-type or tension-type headache with autonomic symptoms — Moderate-High likelihood
  - Anxiety/panic disorder with autonomic symptoms related to work stress — Medium likelihood
  - Pheochromocytoma — Low likelihood (consider if atypical features emerge; not strongly supported by current history)
- Conflict noted: None
